stories.title: Circle Realty Secures 38K SF of New Leases at 14 Penn Plaza
stories.excerpt: Circle Realty Group has closed on 37,600 square feet of new leases in Midtown, Commercial Observer has learned. The two largest deals at 225 West 34th Street, also known as 14 Penn Plaza, were for civil engineering company Bohler Engineering, which expanded from 8,000 square feet to 14,000 square feet, and cybersecurity firm T&M USA, which took 14,000 square feet, according to Circle Realty. Bohler signed a 10-year lease and asking rent in the building was $67 per square foot. The length of T&M’s lease was unclear. “These tenants came to me because we’re at the center of transportation and we have a first-class property,” Circle Realty President Jay Futersak told CO. “Tenants know that what we promised is what we deliver.” Futersak represented his own firm in-house and both tenants in the deals. Smaller recent deals in the building were for accounting and advisory firm Calibre CPA Group, which signed a 10-year, 6,100-square-foot lease and is relocating from 462 Seventh Avenue. Mark Furst and Benjamin Saftler of Kaufman Leasing, the brokerage arm of the Kaufman Organization, handled the deal for the Washington, D.C.-based accounting firm and did not immediately comment. Meanwhile, discrimination law firm Fitapelli & Schaffer is also relocating from 20 Liberty Street to 14 Penn with a new 3,514-square-foot lease. Robert Gallucci of Colliers negotiated on behalf of the law firm and did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Futersak repped ownership in-house in the Calibre and Fitapelli deals. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Circle Realty leased 37,600 SF at 14 Penn Plaza, Midtown Manhattan; $67/SF asking rent.
Bohler Engineering expanded 8K to 14K SF (10-yr); T&M USA took 14K SF.
Professional services firms (Calibre CPA, accounting) relocating within Midtown Manhattan.
stories.summary: Circle Realty closed 37,600 SF of new leases at 225 West 34th Street (14 Penn Plaza) in Midtown Manhattan. Major tenants included civil engineering firm Bohler Engineering (expanding to 14,000 SF on a 10-year lease at $67/SF) and cybersecurity firm T&M USA (14,000 SF). Smaller deals included Calibre CPA Group, a 6,100-SF relocation from nearby 462 Seventh Avenue.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. Office leasing activity signals sustained demand for Midtown professional services space, but does not indicate residential in-migration, population growth, or new job categories that would drive apartment demand in Manhattan or surrounding submarkets.

stories.title: Sunday Summary: Who’s Funding $1.3 Trillion in Data Center Spending?
stories.excerpt: Pluck your average Commercial Observer journalist off the street, shove them in a van, shine a flashlight in their eyes, and say, “Quick — what’s the biggest story in commercial real estate?” nine reporters out of 10 will answer: “Data centers.” At least that’s the case in 2026 after the billions and billions of dollars in investment that have been lavished on the sector. Actually, make that trillion — with a “t.” It’s still a sector that’s largely mysterious and unknown (even the vocabulary of the asset class is new!) so CO was excited last week when San Diego-based Atrium, an AI analytics firm, launched an interactive data platform called “Who Finances America’s Data Centers,” which tracks the money behind the $1.3 trillion (and counting) data center bonanza. What makes Atrium’s platform so fascinating is that it delves into the nitty gritty of individual deals like Coreweave’s $23 billion debt facility from 38 different lenders, and the 24 lenders financing DigitalBridge and IFM’s $20 billion debt facility — but at the same time it examines the breadth of activity of non-bank lenders like PIMCO (which has done $23 billion in originations), or borrowers like Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta and Oracle (five firms that alone account for $223 billion in long-term debt and credit facilities). All this data center activity comes as construction costs have been on the rise. Construction might have slowed down in other sectors, but the explosive growth of data centers has seemingly made up for it, at least according to a recent report from Skanska. “The market is hot and cold right now — hot and warm may be a better way to say it — so what stands out is that we’re seeing a lot of project activity around data centers, semiconductor, life sciences,” said Skanska’s Tom Park. “There’s really a lot of unprecedented demand in the mechanical, electrical, plumbing and steel space driving up lead times and cost.” Moreover, the companies that rely on the proliferation of data cent
bullets: $1.3 trillion in data center investment pipeline being financed by 60+ lenders nationwide.
Coreweave raised $23B debt from 38 lenders; DigitalBridge/IFM $20B from 24 lenders.
PIMCO, non-bank lenders dominating originations; Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta, Oracle major borrowers.
stories.summary: Data center financing has become a major capital market story, with $1.3 trillion in spending being funded through diverse lender pools. Coreweave secured a $23 billion debt facility from 38 lenders, while DigitalBridge and IFM arranged $20 billion across 24 lenders. Non-bank lenders like PIMCO have originated $23 billion, and tech giants (Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta, Oracle) are the primary borrowers driving AI and cloud infrastructure expansion.
stories.impact: Data center mega-projects, particularly in Tier 1 metros (Dallas, Phoenix, Northern Virginia, Austin) and secondary tech hubs, will concentrate high-wage tech and operations jobs in specific corridors. This drives in-migration of tech workers and supporting service labor into these metros, creating strong multifamily demand in submarkets near major data center campuses. Developers should monitor site acquisition and build-to-suit opportunities in data center adjacencies where residential supply remains constrained.

stories.title: Zimmet Law Group Signs 10-Year Lease for 515 Madison Ave.
stories.excerpt: GFP Real Estate announced that Zimmet Law Group P.C. has signed a new office lease for 5,476 square feet at 515 Madison Ave. in Manhattan’s Plaza District. Zimmet Law Group will occupy Suite 603 on the sixth floor of the building under a new 10-year lease, relocating its Manhattan office from 477 Madison Ave. The firm is expected to take occupancy following completion of its new space later this year. Martin McGrath and Kephra Stone of GFP Real Estate represented the landlord in-house. Elliot Zelinger of Savitt Partners represented Zimmet Law Group. “Zimmet Law Group’s decision to make a long-term commitment to 515 Madison Avenue speaks to the continued appeal of the building and the strength of the Plaza District,” said McGrath. “Professional services firms continue to prioritize high-quality, well-located office space, and we’re pleased to welcome Zimmet Law Group to the building.” The post Zimmet Law Group Signs 10-Year Lease for 515 Madison Ave. appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Zimmet Law Group signed 10-year lease for 5,476 SF at 515 Madison Ave, Manhattan.
Relocation from 477 Madison Ave; Plaza District, professional services commitment.
Occupancy expected end-2026 following tenant build-out.
stories.summary: Zimmet Law Group P.C. executed a new 10-year lease for 5,476 SF at 515 Madison Avenue in Manhattan's Plaza District (Suite 603, sixth floor), relocating from 477 Madison Avenue. The lease represents a professional services firm making a long-term commitment to the building, with occupancy expected later in 2026 following tenant improvements.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. Office lease activity in Plaza District does not signal material population in-migration or job creation that would move apartment demand metrics in Manhattan or surrounding markets.

stories.title: Avison Young Recapitalization Provides “War Chest” for Further Growth
stories.excerpt: Avison Young’s newly announced recapitalization does more than deleverage the company’s balance sheet debt-to-EBITDA ratio to less than 3x, reduce debt and preferred equity by nearly 70% and give key financial partners a common equity position, although it accomplishes all of these. “We’re pretty excited,” Avison Young chair and CEO Mark E. Rose told Connect CRE. “This gives us the war chest to do the things that we’re known for”–namely, make strategic acquisitions, broaden the platform’s capabilities and expand the pool of talent through recruitment. “And we have our eyes on targets.” Expected to close in October, the new transaction builds upon the success of the company’s 2024 recapitalization. It also represents a rethinking of how to produce the best outcome for Avison Young’s longtime financial stakeholders as well as the company’s principals.   “It’s kind of simple,” said Rose. “Was it better to take the money and pay these [stakeholders], or was it better to invest and make them multiples of the same money? And after 16 months, that’s what we were able to come to.”  The process of devising this solution began in the spring of 2025, Rose said. bullets: Avison Young recapitalization reduces debt-to-EBITDA to <3x; cuts debt/preferred equity 70%.
Closing expected October 2026; follows successful 2024 recapitalization transaction.
Provides 'war chest' for strategic acquisitions, platform expansion, talent acquisition.
stories.summary: Avison Young announced a recapitalization that deleverages its balance sheet to a debt-to-EBITDA ratio below 3x while reducing debt and preferred equity by nearly 70%. The transaction, expected to close in October, converts financial partners to common equity holders and positions the brokerage firm to make strategic acquisitions, broaden service capabilities, and expand talent. CEO Mark Rose stated the move enables the company to do "the things we're known for."
stories.impact: Signal of increased M&A and platform consolidation activity in the CRE brokerage and advisory space. This does not directly affect multifamily supply, demand, or financing, but indicates capital is flowing toward service providers and intermediaries in the space. Developers may see Avison Young as a more aggressive player in land and development deal sourcing as it expands its platform.

stories.title: Local Owner-Operator Snags Pico-Robertson Apartment Property
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of 1476 S Shenandoah St., a 16-unit multifamily property in Los Angeles. The property sold for $5.3 million, or $334,937 per unit.  “Properties like this rarely become available in Pico-Robertson, especially those that have been held by the same ownership for more than two decades,” said Sam Liberow, senior managing director investments. “After 23 years of ownership, the offering generated six competitive offers, reflecting continued demand for well-located multifamily assets with large floor plans. The buyer plans to renovate units through natural tenant turnover while holding the property as a long-term investment.” Liberow, in Marcus & Millichap’s Encino office, marketed the property on behalf of the seller, 1476 Shenandoah Street LLC. He also procured the buyer, a local owner and operator. Built in 1966, the 17,653-square-foot property is situated on a 0.30-acre parcel in Los Angeles’ Pico-Robertson neighborhood. The conversations behind tomorrow’s apartment deals happen at Connect Apartments on September 22 in LA. Connect with the capital sources, owners, developers, and brokers driving multifamily investment. Learn more and reserve your seat at www.connectapts2026.com. The post Local Owner-Operator Snags Pico-Robertson Apartment Property appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 16-unit multifamily at 1476 S Shenandoah St, Los Angeles sold for $5.3M; $334,937/unit.
Pico-Robertson neighborhood; 1966-built, 17,653 SF on 0.30-acre lot; held 23 years.
Local owner-operator buyer; six competitive offers; plans unit renovation through turnover.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of 1476 South Shenandoah Street, a 16-unit multifamily property in Los Angeles's Pico-Robertson neighborhood, for $5.3 million ($334,937/unit). The 1966-built, 17,653-SF property was held by the same owner for 23 years and generated six competitive offers. The new buyer, a local owner-operator, plans to renovate units through natural tenant turnover while holding as a long-term investment.
stories.impact: Pico-Robertson multifamily assets remain highly competitive and expensive at $335K/unit despite vintage construction. Six bids indicate persistent investor demand for well-located LA multifamily in established neighborhoods, even at high per-unit prices. Developers seeking entry into Pico-Robertson or similarly infill-constrained LA submarkets face significant land cost barriers; attention should shift to land acquisition in adjacent, less-saturated areas or consider development in secondary LA submarkets with better ROI fundamentals.

stories.title: Grocery-Anchored Queens Retail Secures $32M Financing
stories.excerpt: Northmarq’s New York Metro Debt + Equity team, led by Robert Delitsky and Charles Cotsalas, arranged $32 million in financing for Springnex Plaza, a 96,028-square-foot retail property located in the Springfield Gardens neighborhood of Queens. Delitsky and Cotsalas arranged financing on behalf of the owner, Mattone Group Springnex LLC, through Principal Financial Group. “Ownership developed Springnex Plaza in 2000 and they have done a fabulous job maintaining very strong occupancy,” Delitsky said. “Supermarket-anchored shopping centers like Springnex Plaza will continue to attract very strong lender interest in today’s market,” added Cotsalas. Springnex Plaza is a 100% occupied, multi-tenant, grocery-anchored retail center situated on approximately 5.58 acres. Serving the Springfield Gardens community for more than two decades, Springnex Plaza offers a complementary mix of grocery, dining, healthcare and service-oriented tenants. Anchored by Stop & Shop, it’s home to a diverse roster of local and national retailers, including Ashley Stewart, IHOP and Northwell Health. The post Grocery-Anchored Queens Retail Secures $32M Financing appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Springnex Plaza, Queens, secured $32M financing through Principal Financial Group.
96,028 SF grocery-anchored retail in Springfield Gardens; 100% occupied; built 2000.
Anchored by Stop & Shop; Northmarq arranged deal; 5.58-acre parcel.
stories.summary: Northmarq's New York Metro Debt + Equity team, led by Robert Delitsky and Charles Cotsalas, arranged $32 million in financing for Springnex Plaza, a 96,028-SF, grocery-anchored retail property in the Springfield Gardens neighborhood of Queens. The fully occupied, multi-tenant center (built 2000) is anchored by Stop & Shop and includes IHOP, Northwell Health, and local retailers on 5.58 acres. Principal Financial Group provided the debt.
stories.impact: Grocery-anchored retail in Queens continues to attract strong lender interest and refinancing activity, indicating stable cash flow and resilience in outer-borough, necessity-driven retail. Queens remains undersupplied for multifamily, and this asset's stability signals healthy demographic fundamentals and foot traffic in Springfield Gardens. Developers should assess multifamily development opportunities in Queens submarkets proximate to well-performing, well-capitalized retail anchors, as these signal reliable population density and consumer spending.

stories.title: Brixton Capital Launches Multifamily Investment-Management Platform
stories.excerpt: Brixton Capital’s Residential division has launched an integrated multifamily investment-management initiative designed to help institutional investors, family offices, lenders, joint venture partners and other owners improve the performance and value of complex multifamily assets. The initiative combines Brixton’s institutional investment and asset management capabilities with the operating expertise of its affiliate, United Apartment Group. “We see a meaningful opportunity to partner with owners and investment groups that have good real estate but need a different investment-management solution,” said Brixton VP of residential acquisitions Mark Mandala. “There are many multifamily assets where the underlying property remains fundamentally attractive, but the existing sponsor may not have the capital, operating infrastructure or institutional asset-management capabilities required for the next phase of ownership. We believe this is a particularly compelling opportunity because we are not simply offering another property management solution—we can bring together the investment strategy and the execution platform under one roof.” Brixton’s Residential division is particularly focused on multifamily assets where ownership is seeking a new investment-management or operating partner, or where the property requires a broader restructuring of its business plan. bullets: Brixton Capital launched integrated multifamily investment-management platform for institutional investors.
Partners with United Apartment Group operating affiliate; targets underperforming complex assets.

stories.summary: Brixton Capital's Residential division launched an integrated multifamily investment-management platform combining institutional investment and asset management capabilities with the operating expertise of affiliate United Apartment Group. The platform targets institutional investors, family offices, lenders, and owners seeking improved performance on complex multifamily assets where sponsors lack capital, operating infrastructure, or institutional asset-management capabilities. Brixton VP Mark Mandala emphasized opportunities to partner with owners who have "good real estate but need a different investment-management solution."
stories.impact: Rising availability of professional asset-management and restructuring platforms signals consolidation and upgrade activity in multifamily. Developers building value-add properties should recognize that third-party operators and institutional sponsors will increasingly seek to partner with or acquire performing assets. This creates an exit pathway for development-stage sponsors but also competitive pressure on hold times and return thresholds; development timelines and IRR assumptions should reflect the likelihood of third-party management take-over post-stabilization.

stories.title: CoStar Closes $800M Cash Acquisition of New-Home Platform Zonda
stories.excerpt: CoStar Group, a leading provider of online real estate marketplaces, information, analytics and 3D digital twin technology, announced that it has completed its acquisition of Zonda, a new home-construction data, homebuilder software and residential real estate marketplace platform, for $800 million in cash. Zonda’s platform of proprietary lot-level construction and development data, which serves more than 3,000 homebuilders, developers, lenders and suppliers, gives CoStar a foothold in the $400 billion annual U.S. new-home sales market, according to the CoStar announcement. Based in Washington, D.C., Zonda generated approximately $170 million in revenue in 2025. CoStar’s acquisition of the platform was first announced in May. “Zonda has built an exceptional business around information the homebuilding industry relies on every day,” Andy Florance, founder and CEO of CoStar, said in announcing the deal’s closing. “This is a massive market with a sophisticated group of builders, developers, lenders, investors and suppliers that need purpose-built information, analytics and marketing solutions. With the acquisition now complete, we have the opportunity to bring together Zonda’s proprietary new construction data, software and builder relationships with CoStar Group’s technology, analytics and marketplace capabilities.” The deal provides Arlington, Va.-based CoStar with new-home data and analytics from Zonda, which tracks new-home communities, land development, construction activity, home sales and builder operations at the lot level. In addition, Zonda-owned residential marketplaces NewHomeSource.com and Livabl join CoStar’s portfolio, expanding its consumer marketplace business specifically into new construction. bullets: CoStar closed $800M cash acquisition of Zonda; homebuilder software and lot-level data.
Zonda serves 3,000+ homebuilders, developers, lenders, suppliers; $170M 2025 revenue.

stories.summary: CoStar Group completed its $800 million cash acquisition of Zonda, a new home-construction data, homebuilder software, and residential real estate marketplace platform. Zonda serves more than 3,000 homebuilders, developers, lenders, and suppliers and generated approximately $170 million in revenue in 2025. The platform provides proprietary lot-level construction and development data that serves the $400 billion annual U.S. new-home sales market.
stories.impact: CoStar's acquisition of Zonda consolidates critical lot-level and new-construction data visibility under one platform, strengthening CoStar's foothold in residential development ecosystems. Multifamily developers using CoStar's existing platforms will see expanded access to lot-level inventory, pricing, and competitive pipeline data. This could lower information asymmetries for land acquisition and enable faster market-entry decisions, particularly in high-growth metros and secondary markets where lot supply and homebuilder activity signals future apartment demand. Monitor integration of Zonda data into CoStar's core products for development site-selection advantages.

stories.title: Michael Troyanovsky of Regency Development Group: 5 Questions

Since 2020, the developer has been building residential projects in the coastal community near Surfside, Indian Creek and Bal Harbour. Regency has four active projects on the island, including the 33-unit La Maré Regency, the nine-unit La Maré Signature and the 20-unit Bay Harbor Villas. Commercial Observer recently caught up with Michael Troyanovsky, managing partner and vice president of the family company, to discuss the submarket’s success. The following conversation has been edited for length and clarity.   Commercial Observer: Why Bay Harbor Islands? What caught your interest about that submarket? We came to the area, and we really felt like it had the most potential. It was always overlooked. It’s honestly the most amazing hidden gem. It’s surrounded by the most beautiful waters, a little nook in the center of Miami. It’s getting more and more discovered. Since then, we really integrated into the island, and we really got to know the local community, the local governments, because we have to work very closely with them on getting all the projects approved and making sure that it fits the neighborhood and demographic. 33-unit La Maré Regency, 9-unit La Maré Signature, 20-unit Bay Harbor Villas.

stories.summary: Regency Development Group, a family-owned developer, is pursuing a concentrated strategy in Bay Harbor Islands, Florida (population <6,000), a coastal community near Surfside and Bal Harbour. stories.impact: Micro-market concentration strategy by experienced South Florida developer signals undersupply and pent-up demand in exclusive, low-density coastal submarkets near Bal Harbour/Surfside premium corridors. Bay Harbor Islands' constrained zoning (population <6K suggests minimal remaining land) and proximity to ultra-high-net-worth communities create favorable rental demand and pricing power. Developers should assess similarly overlooked, low-density, coastal-adjacent Florida submarkets (Miami-Dade, Broward micro-communities) where land constraints and proximity to strong-performing tourist/luxury retail anchors can support niche, boutique multifamily development with premium economics.

stories.title: JBL Asset Management Buys Retail Condo Near Miami Design District
stories.excerpt: Alta Developers sold off a retail condo near the Miami Design District for $17.3 million, property records show. JBL Asset Management purchased the 25,504-square-foot asset on the ground floor of the Quadro condo building. The property at 3900 Biscayne Boulevard faces train tracks, just east of the Miami Design District, an open-air, luxury mall. Quadro’s retail tenants include The Shade Store, 7th Avenue furniture store and Waterworks plumbing supply store. Hollywood, Fla.-based JBL is marketing a 2,358-square-foot suite as the last remaining retail space at the 407,498-square-foot condo building. Alta Developers completed the 200-unit building in 2019. The purchase comes as the 18-block Design District, one of the country’s highest-grossing upscale malls, is undergoing a major expansion. Earlier this week, its owners, entities tied to Miami-based Craig Robins and LVMH billionaire Bernard Arnault, scored a $125 million construction loan to build a Snøhetta-designed, mixed-use building. The joint venture also launched sales for Fouquet’s condo and hotel development, designed by Pritzker Prize winner David Chipperfield. Representatives for Alta Developers and JBL Asset Management did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: JBL Asset Management purchased 25,504 SF retail condo near Miami Design District for $17.3M.
Ground floor at Quadro condo (407,498 SF building), 3900 Biscayne Boulevard; 2,358 SF suite available.
Tenants: The Shade Store, 7th Avenue furniture, Waterworks plumbing; Design District expansion underway.
stories.summary: JBL Asset Management purchased a 25,504-SF retail condo on the ground floor of the Quadro building near Miami's Design District for $17.3 million. Located at 3900 Biscayne Boulevard (east of the Design District, facing train tracks), the property includes The Shade Store, 7th Avenue furniture, and Waterworks plumbing as tenants, with one remaining 2,358-SF retail suite being marketed. The Design District (18 blocks, one of the country's highest-grossing upscale malls) is undergoing major expansion with a $125M construction loan funding a mixed-use building and Fouquet's condo/hotel by Chipperfield and Snøhetta.
stories.impact: Design District expansion (mixed-use tower, Fouquet's luxury hotel/condo, $125M construction financing) will drive pedestrian traffic, luxury retail demand, and residential in-migration into Edgewater and adjacent Miami neighborhoods. Developers should acquire multifamily land in Edgewater and Little Haiti (Wynwood corridor access) proximate to Design District as expansion anchors strong rental demand growth. Retail properties near Design District will see value uplift and lease rate expansion; multifamily positioned 0.5–1.5 miles north/northwest will capture overflow demand at lower land and construction costs than premium districts.
